root_cause: The aria-activedescendant attribute is incorrectly set to the item's data-value (label) instead of the element's id, causing assistive technologies to announce the wrong active option during arrow navigation.
repair_strategy: In src/controllers/navigationController.js, update the assignment of aria-activedescendant to use the list item's id attribute rather than its dataset.value.
expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowDown and ArrowUp keystrokes will correctly update aria-activedescendant to reference the active option element's ID, enabling screen readers to announce the highlighted suggestion as intended.
functional_risks: Any external code that mistakenly reads aria-activedescendant expecting the item's label would need adjustment, but the attribute is spec-defined to hold an ID reference; no functional impact is expected within this codebase.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown, aria-activedescendant on #store must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1' and aria-selected on that element must be true.
Pressing ArrowUp from the first suggestion should wrap to the last suggestion and set aria-activedescendant accordingly.
Form submission with Enter should still populate the input with the selected suggestion's value.
